_comment: Registry for the ecosystem dev-script sync (distribute_scripts.py, ADR D-013; vendored layout ADR D-014). The canonical sources are the 'src' paths under kriegerdataforge-cicd/scripts/common/; each is vendored byte-identical to every repo in 'repos' at its 'dest' path under scripts/kdf_scripts/ -- a vendor directory that every tenant's kdf-fmt.toml and ruff config EXCLUDES, so cicd alone governs the style of what it ships. 'deletes' are superseded paths removed by the same sync PR (the pre-1.1.0 flat scripts/ layout). 'makefile_patch' rewrites script paths + the canonical ci-version-check recipe; 'kdf_fmt_patch' appends the vendor-dir exclude to kdf-fmt.toml; a repo's optional 'ruff_config' names the file (ruff.toml or pyproject.toml) that gets the same exclude. check mode reports drift; distribute mode opens one PR per drifted repo (never auto-merges). See docs/features/version-scripts-sync.md.
_pretested_comment: A file entry with "pretested": true is a byte identical copy that cicd's own suite tests the way every repo uses it, so a sync PR whose changes are only such copies carries [skip ci] and runs no CI (ADR D-047). The flag is opt in, an entry without it never skips. Patches of a repo's own files and deletes never skip either.

files._comment: The shared mutation engine (ADR D-040). Only the repos that run hand written Python mutants carry it, so the entry names them in 'repos' and every other repo is left without it. Each repo keeps its tables in mutation_tests/ and its unit settings in mutation_tests/__init__.py. Not pretested (ADR D-047), cicd tests the engine but never against a repo's own tables, so a sync that changes it runs the repo's CI.

requirements_patch._comment: Canonical Python toolchain declarations merged into every repo's requirements-dev.in. The vendored scripts are stdlib-only and need nothing to RUN; this declares the tools that LINT and FORMAT them, so local dev and CI agree. kdf-fmt tracks main (D-054): the style lanes read its ref from requirements-dev.in and make ci-style refreshes it before each check, so no pin moves again. A package already declared differently fails the sync as NEEDS MANUAL ATTENTION -- never rewritten. 'kdf_fmt_ref' is checked read-only against .github/workflows/ci.yml, where a repo passes it only as an override and most pass none, and never written (pushing workflow files needs the 'workflow' token scope).

repos._skip_reason: The terraform repo runs no kdf-fmt lane (its ADR D-010). Its only Python is the three vendored scripts, which its kdf-fmt.toml excluded, so the lane checked zero files, and keeping it meant adding a package token to the repo that holds the Vercel token. It carries no kdf-fmt.toml to patch and needs no requirements-dev.in pinning a formatter it never runs.

The auth UI runs no kdf-fmt lane (its ADR D-008). Its only Python is the three vendored scripts, which its kdf-fmt.toml excluded, so the lane checked zero files. It carries no kdf-fmt.toml to patch and needs no requirements-dev.in pinning a formatter it never runs.
kdf-fmt is the package this pin POINTS AT; pinning it here would make the repo depend on itself, and it has no kdf_fmt_ref in ci.yml because it is the formatter, not a consumer of one.

_excluded_notes: kriegerdataforge-cicd is the SOURCE — its scripts/common/ copies ARE the canonical, so it is not a sync target (no self-PRs; its own Makefile calls scripts/common/check_version.py directly and its kdf-fmt config governs the canonical style). Both registries include kriegerdataforge-fmt, the kit one since 2026-09-29. The 4 template repos are included so a /generate'd repo is born with current scripts AND the vendor-dir excludes. Per-repo scripts/version_targets.json manifests are NOT synced and deliberately stay OUTSIDE scripts/kdf_scripts/ (tenant-owned config, see version_targets.py). A scripts-sync PR does not bump VERSION: the central scripts/common/check_version.py exempts PRs that touch only these dest+delete paths (plus Makefile / kdf-fmt.toml / ruff.toml / pyproject.toml, on chore/scripts-sync-* branches only) — ADR D-013, mirroring the kit's ADR D-001 option B.
